questions.title: API Gateway Pattern
questions.question: What is an API Gateway and what problems does it solve in a microservices architecture?

sections.title: What the Interviewer Wants to Hear
sections.content:
- **Single entry point for all client requests — routes to downstream services**
- **Cross-cutting concerns: auth, rate limiting, SSL termination, logging**
- **Spring Cloud Gateway: routes, filters, predicates**
- **BFF (Backend for Frontend): separate gateway per client type (mobile vs web)**
- **Risk: single point of failure — must be highly available and stateless**
- **Don't put business logic in the gateway — keep it thin and routing-focused**

sections.title: Interview Answer
sections.content:
An API Gateway is the single entry point for all client requests. Instead of clients knowing about 10 different microservice URLs, they talk to the gateway, which routes requests to the appropriate service. This solves multiple problems: clients don't need to track service URLs, you can do auth/rate-limiting once at the gateway instead of in every service, and you can do protocol translation (HTTP/2 externally, HTTP/1.1 internally).

Spring Cloud Gateway is the Spring ecosystem's gateway built on Reactor — it's non-blocking and handles routing via predicates (path matching, header matching) and filters (add/remove headers, rate limiting, circuit breaking).

The main risk is that the gateway becomes a bottleneck or single point of failure. Keep it stateless, deploy it as multiple instances, and keep business logic out of it — it should only route and apply cross-cutting concerns.
